'''Maria-Elena Torres-Padilla''' is a Mexican [[biologist]] who is the Director of the Stem Cell Center,<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.helmholtz-munich.de/en/stem-cells | title=Helmholtz Munich | date=3 December 2025 }}</ref> the Director of the Institute for [[Epigenetics]] and [[Stem cell|Stem Cells]] (IES),<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.helmholtz-munich.de/en/ies | title=Helmholtz Munich | date=20 December 2023 }}</ref> and a Group Leader at the [[Helmholtz Zentrum München]], Germany.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.helmholtz-munich.de/en/ies/research-groups/torres-padilla-lab | title=Helmholtz Munich }}</ref>

==Education==
From 1994 until 1998, Torres-Padilla completed her undergraduate studies at the Faculty of Sciences of the [[National Autonomous University of Mexico]] in [[Mexico]] and earned her Ph.D. from the [[Pasteur Institute|Institut Pasteur]] in [[Paris]] in 2002.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.sfb1064.med.uni-muenchen.de/personen/professoren/torres_padilla/index.html | title=Torres-Padilla, Maria Elena – SFB 1064 – LMU Munich }}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Member/Torres-Padilla_Maria-Elena | title=Academy of Europe: Torres-Padilla Maria-Elena }}</ref>

==Career and research==
Between 2002 and 2006, she was a [[postdoctoral fellow]] at The Gurdon Institute, [[University of Cambridge]], UK, after which she worked as a permanent scientist under Laszlo Tora's supervision.<ref>{{cite journal | doi=10.1038/nature05458 | title=Histone arginine methylation regulates pluripotency in the early mouse embryo | date=2007 | last1=Torres-Padilla | first1=Maria-Elena | last2=Parfitt | first2=David-Emlyn | last3=Kouzarides | first3=Tony | last4=Zernicka-Goetz | first4=Magdalena | journal=Nature | volume=445 | issue=7124 | pages=214–218 | pmid=17215844 | pmc=3353120 | bibcode=2007Natur.445..214T }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | url=https://ijdb.ehu.eus/article/052073mt?doi=10.1387/ijdb.052073mt | doi=10.1387/ijdb.052073mt | title=Dynamic distribution of the replacement histone variant H3.3 in the mouse oocyte and preimplantation embryos | date=2006 | last1=Torres-Padilla | first1=Maria-Elena | last2=Bannister | first2=Andrew J. | last3=Hurd | first3=Paul J. | last4=Kouzarides | first4=Tony | last5=Zernicka-Goetz | first5=Magdalena | journal=The International Journal of Developmental Biology | volume=50 | issue=5 | pages=455–461 | pmid=16586346 | url-access=subscription }}</ref>

The primary objective of Torres-Padilla's research activities is to comprehend the manner in which epigenetic information controls the shifts in cellular identity and [[cellular reprogramming]]. This is crucial in comprehending [[pluripotent]] stem cell biology, particularly their development and origin. The work also endeavors to gain insight into the early stages of [[embryonic development]], [[human reproduction]], [[fertility]], and stem cell biology from a broader perspective.<ref>{{cite journal | doi=10.1038/s41588-017-0016-5 | title=A molecular roadmap for the emergence of early-embryonic-like cells in culture | date=2018 | last1=Rodriguez-Terrones | first1=Diego | last2=Gaume | first2=Xavier | last3=Ishiuchi | first3=Takashi | last4=Weiss | first4=Amélie | last5=Kopp | first5=Arnaud | last6=Kruse | first6=Kai | last7=Penning | first7=Audrey | last8=Vaquerizas | first8=Juan M. | last9=Brino | first9=Laurent | last10=Torres-Padilla | first10=Maria-Elena | journal=Nature Genetics | volume=50 | issue=1 | pages=106–119 | pmid=29255263 | pmc=5755687 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | url=https://www.nature.com/articles/s41580-023-00599-7 | doi=10.1038/s41580-023-00599-7 | title=Heterochromatin definition and function | date=2023 | last1=Bell | first1=Oliver | last2=Burton | first2=Adam | last3=Dean | first3=Caroline | last4=Gasser | first4=Susan M. | last5=Torres-Padilla | first5=Maria-Elena | journal=Nature Reviews Molecular Cell Biology | volume=24 | issue=10 | pages=691–694 | pmid=37069331 | url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | url=https://ijdb.ehu.eus/article/200176jc | doi=10.1387/ijdb.200176jc | title=Epigenetic control of cell fate - an interview with Maria-Elena Torres-Padilla | date=2021 | last1=Chimal-Monroy | first1=Jesús | last2=Escalante-Alcalde | first2=Diana | journal=The International Journal of Developmental Biology | volume=65 | issue=1–2–3 | pages=163–169 | pmid=32930362 | doi-access=free }}</ref>

Torres-Padilla is an [[editorial board]] member of [[Science (journal)|Science]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=Editors and Advisory Boards |url=https://www.science.org/content/page/editors-and-advisory-boards |access-date=2024-08-30 |website=science.org}}</ref> [[Development (journal)|Development]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=Editors and Board |url=https://journals.biologists.com/dev/pages/edboard |access-date=2024-08-30 |website=journals.biologists.com}}</ref> [[Genes & Development]],<ref>{{cite web | url=https://genesdev.cshlp.org/site/misc/edboard.xhtml | title=Genes & Development – Genes & Development Editorial Board }}</ref> and EMBO Reports
